quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: [While] the bell rings, all students must leave the building quickly.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause showing the exact moment an action should start.
quests.explanation: 'When' introduces the exact moment something happens, not 'While,' which describes an ongoing action.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Please stay in your seats [when] the teacher gives further instructions.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause meaning 'up to the moment that' something happens.
quests.explanation: 'Until' means 'up to the point when,' fitting staying seated up to a moment, not 'when.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: [While] I finish grading these papers, I'll send you the results.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause meaning 'immediately after.'
quests.explanation: 'As soon as' means 'immediately after,' not 'While,' which describes two simultaneous actions.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: [When] the manager is in a meeting, please don't interrupt her at all.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause describing an action happening during another action.
quests.explanation: 'While' describes an action happening at the same time as another ongoing one, not 'When.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: [While] you finish the report, send it directly to the client right away.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause meaning 'at the moment that' something is completed.
quests.explanation: 'When' shows the exact moment an action is completed, not 'While,' which describes simultaneous actions.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: We can't submit the proposal [when] everyone approves the final draft.
quests.hint: Think about a time clause meaning 'up to the point that.'
quests.explanation: 'Until' shows an action can't happen before a certain point is reached, not 'when.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: All passports [must shown] be at the border before crossing into the country.
quests.hint: Passive with modals follows the pattern modal + be + past participle, with nothing missing.
quests.explanation: Passive with modals needs 'be' between the modal and the past participle: 'must be shown,' not 'must shown.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: This luggage tag [should removed] be before the flight leaves the gate.
quests.hint: This passive structure needs the helping verb 'be' inserted between the modal and the participle.
quests.explanation: Passive with modals needs 'be': 'should be removed,' not 'should removed.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Tickets [can booked] be at least two weeks in advance for the best prices.
quests.hint: Don't skip 'be' when combining a modal verb with a passive past participle.
quests.explanation: Passive with modals needs 'be': 'can be booked,' not 'can booked.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: These old photographs [should kept] be somewhere safe and dry at all times.
quests.hint: Remember that passive modals always include 'be' right before the past participle.
quests.explanation: Passive with modals needs 'be': 'should be kept,' not 'should kept.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: This family recipe [has passed] down for four generations now in our family.
quests.hint: The passive present perfect needs 'has been' plus the past participle, with nothing missing.
quests.explanation: The passive present perfect uses 'has been' + past participle: 'has been passed down,' not just 'has passed.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: Important decisions like this [must discussed] be by the whole family together.
quests.hint: Check that 'be' appears between the modal verb and the past participle here.
quests.explanation: Passive with modals needs 'be': 'must be discussed,' not 'must discussed.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: The cashier asked me [did I want] a paper or plastic bag for my groceries.
quests.hint: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' plus normal statement word order, not question word order.
quests.explanation: Reported yes/no questions need 'if' and statement order: 'if I wanted,' not the inverted 'did I want.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She asked me [had I found] the right size for the jacket I wanted.
quests.hint: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' plus normal statement word order, not inverted question order.
quests.explanation: Reported questions need 'if' and statement word order: 'if I had found,' not the inverted 'had I found.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: The manager wanted to know what time [does the store close] on weekends.
quests.hint: In reported questions, normal statement word order is used, not question word order.
quests.explanation: Reported questions use statement order (subject + verb): 'the store closes,' not the inverted question form.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: The waiter asked us [were we ready] to order our meal yet.
quests.hint: Reported yes/no questions use 'if' plus normal statement word order.
quests.explanation: Reported questions need 'if' and statement order: 'if we were ready,' not the inverted 'were we ready.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She asked me what kind of food [did I like] the most.
quests.hint: In reported questions, normal statement word order is used, with a tense shift to the past.
quests.explanation: Reported questions use statement order with a tense shift: 'I liked,' not the inverted 'did I like.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: He wanted to know how much [did the dessert cost] at that fancy restaurant.
quests.hint: In reported questions, normal statement word order is used, often with a tense shift to the past.
quests.explanation: Reported questions use statement order with a tense shift: 'the dessert cost,' not the inverted question form.

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If I [didn't lose] my phone, I wouldn't have missed your important call.
quests.hint: Third conditional uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause to talk about an unreal past situation, not the simple past.
quests.explanation: The third conditional uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause: 'hadn't lost,' not the simple past 'didn't lose.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If she had backed up her files, she [wouldn't lose] all that important data.
quests.hint: The main clause of a third conditional uses 'would have' plus the past participle, not just 'would.'
quests.explanation: The result clause of a third conditional uses 'would have' + past participle: 'wouldn't have lost,' not 'wouldn't lose.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If the software [was] updated sooner, the system wouldn't have crashed last week.
quests.hint: Third conditional uses the past perfect (passive here) in the 'if' clause, not the simple past.
quests.explanation: The 'if' clause of a third conditional uses the past perfect, here passive: 'had been updated,' not 'was updated.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If he [went] to the doctor sooner, he would have recovered much faster.
quests.hint: Third conditional uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause to discuss an unreal past situation, not the simple past.
quests.explanation: The third conditional's 'if' clause uses the past perfect for an unreal past situation: 'had gone,' not 'went.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If she had rested more, she [wouldn't have been] so exhausted right now.
quests.hint: This links a past condition to a present result, a mixed conditional pattern, so the result is about now.
quests.explanation: When a past condition affects a present state, the result clause uses 'would' + base verb: 'wouldn't be,' not 'wouldn't have been.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: If I [knew] about the side effects, I wouldn't have taken that medicine at all.
quests.hint: Third conditional uses the past perfect in the 'if' clause, not the simple past.
quests.explanation: The 'if' clause of a third conditional requires the past perfect: 'had known,' not the simple past 'knew.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: The concert [must] have ended already, because the lights are off and the doors are locked.
quests.hint: Modals of speculation about the past need 'have' plus the past participle, not the bare modal alone.
quests.explanation: Past speculation needs 'modal + have + past participle': 'must have ended,' not just 'must ended.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She didn't answer her phone; she [might] been at the cinema with friends.
quests.hint: Modals of speculation about the past need 'have' plus the past participle.
quests.explanation: Past speculation needs 'have': 'might have been,' not just 'might been.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: He knew every detail about the film, so he [must] watched it already.
quests.hint: Speculating about a past event needs 'have' added before the past participle.
quests.explanation: Past speculation needs 'have': 'must have watched,' not just 'must watched.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: She hasn't replied to my message; she [might] been busy at work all day.
quests.hint: This modal of speculation requires 'have' linking it to the past participle.
quests.explanation: Speculating about the past requires 'have': 'might have been,' never 'might been.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: He knew exactly what I meant, so he [must] read my email very carefully.
quests.hint: Don't drop 'have' when speculating about something that already happened.
quests.explanation: Past speculation needs 'have': 'must have read,' not just 'must read.'

quests.instruction: Correct the grammatical error in the sentence.
quests.passage: I'm not sure why she left early; she [might] had an emergency at home.
quests.hint: Modals of speculation about the past need 'have' plus the past participle, with both words present correctly.
quests.explanation: Past speculation needs 'might have had,' combining 'have' with the past participle 'had,' not just 'might had.'
